newsitem.title: USA: GTECH says gets five-year contract with Ky..
newsitem.headline: GTECH says gets five-year contract with Ky..

text.p: GTECH Holdings Corp said Monday the Kentucky Lottery Corp has been authorized to enter into a new five-year contract under which the company will provide on-line services and equipment for the lottery.
The company was not immediately able to dislose the dollar value of the contract.
The company said that under the new agreement, it will replace the lottery's existing on-line system with new system equipment, software, and terminals.
The company said it will also provide services for the lottery including system and terminal installation and maintenance, communications management, retailer training, and marketing support.
The company said the contract, which can be extended by the lottery for up to five additional years, is subject to final regulatory approval.
The company said it was invited to negotiate a new contract after the lottery accepted Automated Wagering International Inc's withdrawal of its proposal.
The company was not immediately able to provide details on that proposal.
The company said it has been providing on-line services and equipment for the state since 1989.
A company spokesman declined to disclose the dollar value of the contract, but said local newspapers are reporting its value at $48 million.
The spokesman said the Kentucky Lottery Corp received its authorization from the state of Kentucky.
The spokesman said the company competed in September 1995 for the contract against Automated Wagering International, a subsidiary of Video Lottery Technologies Inc.
The spokesman said the state awarded the contract to Automated Wagering, and after 11 months on negotiations, Automated withdrew its proposal.
The spokesman said he could not say why Automated withdrew its proposal.
